entries.paragraph_1: “직스캐드 AX로 경쟁 제품을 대체하고 AI를 넣어 한 단계 나아갔다면, 다음은 설계 생태계를 바꾸는 단계입니다. 국산 컴퓨터지원설계(CAD)의 기술력과 생태계를 키워 국내 기업의 외산 소프트웨어(SW) 의존도를 낮추겠습니다.” 최종복 직스테크놀로지 대표는 최근 본지와 인터뷰에서 이같이 강조했다. 국내 고객과 협력해 확보한 실무 도면을 인공지능(AI)에 학습시키고, 이를 설계 현장에 맞는 제품 경쟁력으로 발전시키겠다는 구상이다. 직스테크놀로지는 외산 CAD 제품을 유통하며 쌓은 경험과 수익을 자체 개발에 투자해 지난 2022년 직스캐드 첫 버전을 출시했다. 그간 연구·개발(R&D)에 300억원 이상을 투입했고, 한화오션·삼성물산·현대스틸·국방과학연구소 등 대기업과 공공기관으로 고객 기반을 넓히고 있다. 국산 CAD '직스캐드 AX', AI 공간 설계 플랫폼 '직스 스페이스', 건설현장 관제 플랫폼 '다이브' 등을 개발하고 있다. 최 대표는 “대기업은 단순히 저렴하다고 제품을 도입하지 않고 수개월간 테스트와 검토를 거친다”며 “최근 국내 대기업과 중견기업이 외산 CAD에서 직스 CAD로 바꾸기 시작했다는 것은 이 같은 과정을 모두 통과했다는 점에서 의미가 있다”고 말했다. 최 대표가 내세운 기술 자산은 실무 도면의 확보 규모와 이를 활용한 AI 학습 경험이다. AI 공간 설계 플랫폼 '직스 스페이스'는 10만 장 이상의 도면을 학습한 모델을 활용한다. 외산 경쟁사보다 국내 고객의 도면을 많이 확보해 자체 AI 모델에 학습시켜 왔다는 설명이다. 최 대표는 “데이터는 양뿐 아니라 품질이 매우 중요하다”며 “고객이 현업에서 사용하는 고품질 도면을 자체 모델에 계속 학습시켜 실제 설계 업무에 필요한 성능을 높이고 있다”고 설명했다. 이어 “국내 산업 현장의 도면 데이터와 자체 AI 기술을 바탕으로 국산 CAD 생태계를 키워가겠다”고 덧붙였다. 특히 직스테크놀로지는 설계 분야 AI 전환(AX)에 속도를 내고 있다. AI가 종이·이미지 도면을 인식해 수정 가능한 설계 데이터로 바꾸고, 이를 2D·3D 공간 구성과 시뮬레이션에 활용하도록 돕는다. 확보한 시간은 더 다양한 설계안을 검토하고 공간의 품질을 높이는 데 활용할 수 있다. 최 대표는 “기획과 실시설계에 시간이 많이 들어가면 디자인 품질을 높일 시간이 부족해진다”며 “더 많은 대안을 시뮬레이션하고 사람이 더 나은 공간을 선택하도록 돕는 것이 AX의 가치”라고 설명했다. 도면 보안도 제품 경쟁력의 중요한 축이다. 국정원의 국가정보보안기본지침, 방위사업청의 방위산업보안업무훈 등과 같은 고객사 보안 요구에 맞춰 기능을 추가 개발한 바 있다. 또한 이외에도 고객사들과 협업 과정에서 도면 공유를 통제하고 외부 유출 시 열람을 제한하는 기능에도 투자하고 있다. 최 대표는 “기업이 수개월, 수년간 투자해 만든 도면에는 수많은 노하우가 담겨 있다”며 “협업 과정의 유출을 최소화하고 도면이 외부로 나갔더라도 열람을 제한하는 등 보안 기능 강화에 힘을 쏟고 있다”고 말했다. 회사는 글로벌 사업 확대 발판 마련을 위해 기업공개(IPO)를 준비하고 있다. 상장 주관사 실사를 마쳤으며, 2027년 거래소 상장 심사 청구와 2027~2028년 상장을 목표로 준비하고 있다. 최 대표는 “글로벌 진출을 앞당길 자금을 확보하고 해외 고객에게 한국 상장사라는 신뢰를 주기 위해 상장을 추진한다”고 설명했다. 이어 “직스 스페이스의 연내 정식 출시를 추진하고, 내년 1월 CES 2027에서 글로벌 론칭에 나설 계획”이라면서 “미국·일본·베트남 등에서는 사업·기술 협력을 추진하는 등 글로벌 사업에 속도를 내겠다”고 덧붙였다. 강성전 기자 castlekang@etnews.com

entries.title: South Korean president calls for renewed talks with North Korea, lasting peace
entries.paragraph_1: Beijing, Nov. 19 (SANA) South Korean President Lee Jae-Myung on Thursday called for renewed dialogue with North Korea to formally end the decades-long conflict on the Korean Peninsula , saying lasting peace was essential to stability and prosperity across the Asia-Pacific region.
entries.paragraph_2: Speaking at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation ( APEC ) summit in Shenzhen, China, Lee expressed hope that talks with Pyongyang could resume and lead to a permanent peace arrangement, according to Yonhap News Agency. “We hope that the door to dialogue with North Korea will reopen, leading to discussions on ending the long-standing war on the Korean Peninsula and establishing a permanent peace regime,” Lee said. He reaffirmed Seoul’s commitment to achieving lasting peace on the peninsula and urged regional countries to support diplomatic efforts toward that goal. Addressing economic challenges, Lee warned that disruptions to the global trading system and mounting uncertainty required closer cooperation among Asia-Pacific economies . He said recent geopolitical crises had highlighted the region’s economic interdependence, with disruptions in one country capable of rapidly affecting neighboring economies. Lee called for stronger protection of the multilateral trading system and greater regional cooperation to stabilize supply chains and strengthen economic resilience. His remarks come as South Korea and the United States seek to revive diplomatic engagement with North Korea amid continuing tensions over Pyongyang’s nuclear program. Speculation has also grown over a possible meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un on the sidelines of the APEC summit, although a South Korean presidential official said such a meeting remained uncertain. The Korean War, fought from 1950 to 1953, ended in an armistice rather than a formal peace treaty, leaving the two Koreas technically at war.

entries.title: Trump, Xi and Putin’s Shenzhen face-to-face meeting proves that in-person summits still matter - Monocle
entries.paragraph_1: Today’s trilateral summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin might be as significant as the Yalta Conference in 1945, in which the three great Allies carved up the world map after the Second World War. But it could just as easily be a repeat of Anchorage : Trump and Putin’s meaningless meet-and-greet in Alaska last year.
entries.paragraph_2: The context of economic discussion is what lubricates this particular ménage à trois. Xi is not hosting his counterparts in Beijing – a setting that would lend a political overtone – but in Shenzhen . This week, China’s tech hub is dazzling crowds with laser-light shows and more than 100 Fortune 500 CEOs have flown into the city. Interestingly, the roster for the summit comprises “member economies” rather than states, so Hong Kong and Taiwan are able to participate. But the frenzy will reach a crescendo today as the leaders of China, Russia and the US retreat from the city to the Qilin Mountain Villa: a location that feels markedly different from San Francisco, Lima and Busan, which hosted the past three bilateral Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (Apec) summits with Xi.

entries.paragraph_2: Lee Sang-ki, THE AsiaN, Korea Former South Korean Justice Minister Cho Kuk was denied entry to Japan at Tokyo’s Haneda Airport on November 17 while traveling to attend an academic seminar. Japanese authorities did not publicly state a reason, though his previous visit to Dokdo and criminal record have drawn speculation. The South Korean government expressed regret and requested preventive measures. The incident coincided with a summit between President Lee Jae-myung and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. Although Cho is politically close to Lee’s administration, his nationalist positions and criticism of Japan make him a potentially uncomfortable figure for Tokyo. The episode highlights persistent diplomatic sensitivities beneath improving bilateral cooperation.

entries.title: Abe cites S. Korea’s potential violations of N. Korea sanctions as reasons for export controls
entries.paragraph_1: In connection with Japan’s adoption of export controls in retaliation for a South Korean court’s ruling that Japanese companies must pay damages to victims of forced labor, Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe provocatively suggested that this was because South Korea may not comply with sanctions against North Korea. Abe appears to have linked North Korea to his restrictions on the exports of three materials used to manufacture semiconductors in an attempt to defuse criticism, some of it inside Japan, that the export controls were an excessive step.
entries.paragraph_2: When asked about the reason for tightening restrictions on exports to South Korea during an appearance on Fuji Television on Sunday, Abe cited “inappropriate issues” and said that South Korea needs to thoroughly comply with sanctions against North Korea. When the Japanese government imposed the retaliatory measures on July 4, it provided two reasons: the lack of trust in its relationship with South Korea and the occurrence of “inappropriate issues in connection with managing exports.” While Tokyo didn’t provide a detailed explanation of what those “inappropriate issues” were, Abe’s remarks hint that they’re connected with North Korea.

entries.title: South Korea's $1 Trillion Export Phenomenon | Armstrong Economics
entries.paragraph_1: South Korea has surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports, becoming only the fourth country in history to reach that milestone, joining the United States, Germany, and China. This is a country that emerged from the Korean War devastated, impoverished, and dependent upon foreign assistance. In the 1960s, Koreans were exporting wigs made from human hair, squid, pig bristles, and whatever else they could sell to earn foreign currency. Today, they are producing the semiconductors powering the global artificial intelligence revolution. This is what happens when a nation develops its productive economy instead of expecting government spending to manufacture prosperity.
entries.paragraph_2: Korean exports have increased more than 36,000-fold since 1948. As recently as 1964, annual exports were only $100 million. They crossed $1 trillion on November 19, 2026, and are projected to reach $1.17 trillion by year-end. The transformation did not happen overnight. South Korea developed steelmaking, shipbuilding, automobiles, electronics, and eventually advanced semiconductors. Its companies invested in manufacturing capabilities that could compete internationally. Samsung, Hyundai, and SK hynix became global industrial powers because they produced goods that consumers and businesses around the world wanted to purchase.

entries.title: Who Makes Bobcat Tractors And Where Are They Manufactured?
entries.paragraph_1: Bobcat traces its origins to North Dakota, United States, where the Melroe Manufacturing Company was established in 1947. The company initially manufactured agricultural equipment and introduced the world's first skid-steer loader in 1960. The Bobcat brand was trademarked in 1962, although it only officially became Bobcat Company in 2000. Today, its product range extends across several categories of construction and agricultural machinery, including loaders, excavators, and compact tractors. Despite its American roots, Bobcat's compact tractors have an international manufacturing arrangement.
entries.paragraph_2: Bobcat compact tractors are manufactured by South Korean agricultural machinery company Daedong, which also sells tractors under its Kioti brand . It manufactures Bobcat's compact tractor lineup in South Korea before shipping them to the United States for assembly. Bobcat handles the final stage of manufacturing at its Statesville facility in North Carolina, where the tractors are assembled for the U.S. market. The companies have maintained their partnership through original equipment manufacturer (OEM) agreements. Meanwhile, Bobcat is owned by South Korea's Doosan Group, which acquired the company in 2007.
